answer: Payout deduplication by similarity treats near-identical answers as one. A grading kernel compares each epoch's answers by structure and argument, not just wording; when seats overlap above a 0.4 score, the cluster earns a single reward split evenly among its authors. A farm of 50 templated personas collects 2% each of one payout while every seat still pays its own bond and fees. Swapping synonyms only changes surface pigment, so escaping the cluster needs genuinely separate reasoning per seat, which cannot be drawn from one shared vault of templates.
